title: Ring buffer sizing + dead-code filter removal
context: PRD-V2-056 had a side investigation into wrong_frame_count events. The investigation confirmed: (a) all 6 Reolink cameras decode at exactly 2 fps; (b) the ring buffer default of 180 frames (= 90s at 2fps, holding ~2.8 GB of PNGs) is wildly over-provisioned because the only consumer (alert handler) asks for n=4 frames; (c) the offset_seconds=6 mtime filter in frame_capture.get_recent_frames() is dead code because mtime is save-time (set inside _save_frames within microseconds), not decode-time. Note: this PRD does NOT change the gate's behavior when fewer than 4 frames are returned - the gate still rejects the alert at line 879 with wrong_frame_count. Operator decision (2026-09-18): shrink the ring and drop the dead filter; gate contract stays.
in_scope: infra/frame_capture.py: change RING_SIZE_DEFAULT from 180 to 12, keep gate contract (4-frame minimum) untouched.
infra/frame_capture.py: remove the dead offset_seconds mtime filter in module-level get_recent_frames().
listener/daemon.py: drop the now-meaningless offset_seconds kwarg in the alert handler.
tests/test_frame_capture.py: update / remove tests that assert the offset_seconds filter behavior, and any test that consumes ring-size directly via PersistentRTSPReader(ring_size=...).
tests/test_frame_capture.py: keep the existing get_recent_frames tests that only assert n-frame tail semantics.
out_of_scope: infra/gate.py: NO change. 4-frame minimum stays. wrong_frame_count still rejects the alert.
Decoder / RTSP transport logic: NO change.

stories.title: Shrink ring buffer from 180 to 12 frames
stories.description:
Reduce RING_SIZE_DEFAULT constant from 180 to 12. Each PIL.Image in the deque occupies ~2.64 MB raw bytes (1280x720 RGB), so shrinking 180 -> 12 reclaims ~440 MB per camera. Across 6 cameras (BACK, FRONT, OUTSIDE_BACK_SOLAR, OUTSIDE_FRONT_GARAGE, OUTSIDE_FRONT_POWER, OUTSIDE_FRONT_SOLAR) that is ~2.5 GB total. The gate contract (4 frames minimum) stays unchanged at infra/gate.py. Justification: 2 fps decode rate * 12 frames = 6 seconds of buffer, which is 2 seconds more than the 4-frame minimum the gate requires. Verified via /debug/rtsp that all 6 cameras decode at 2.0 fps. No production code path reads deeper than 4 frames from the ring.

Also update stale documentation references:
- README.md line 18: '180-frame lossless-ish JPEG ring per camera' -> '12-frame lossless PNG ring per camera'.
- docs/V2-LOGIC-FLOW.md line 137: '180-frame rolling buffer (deque(maxlen=180))' -> '12-frame rolling buffer (deque(maxlen=12))'.

stories.title: Remove dead offset_seconds=6 mtime filter
stories.description:
Module-level get_recent_frames() (infra/frame_capture.py:680-704) filters PNG paths by os.path.getmtime(p) >= now - 6. But mtime is set inside _save_frames when the PNG is written to disk, and all 4 paths are written in the same call within microseconds. So mtimes are effectively identical, and the cutoff check 'ages >=6s' always passes. Drop the filter and the offset_seconds parameter entirely. Update the alert handler call site at listener/daemon.py:444.

Also update stale documentation references:
- docs/V2-LOGIC-FLOW.md lines 57, 119, 131: three references to offset_seconds=6 and the mtime filter must be removed/replaced. After fix, the diagram should show get_recent_frames(camera_id, n=4) without offset_seconds, and the 'filter by mtime' step disappears.
